facts.statement: Oxalaia lived during the Cenomanian stage of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Cretaceous, (Cenomanian)

facts.statement: Oxalaia lived in what is now the Northeast Region of Brazil between 100.5 and 93.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Oxalaia (in reference to the African deity Oxalá) is a genus of spinosaurid dinosaur that lived in what is now the Northeast Region of Brazil during the Cenomanian stage of the Late Cretaceous period, sometime between 100.5 and 93.9 million years ago.

facts.statement: Oxalaia fossils were discovered in 1999 on Cajual Island within the Alcântara Formation.
facts.quote: Its fossils were found in 1999 on Cajual Island in the rocks of the Alcântara Formation

facts.statement: Oxalaia was described in 2011 by Alexander Kellner and colleagues.
facts.quote: The remains of Oxalaia were described in 2011 by Brazilian palaeontologist Alexander Kellner and colleagues

facts.statement: The described species is Oxalaia quilombensis.
facts.quote: who assigned the specimens to a new genus containing one species, Oxalaia quilombensis

facts.statement: Oxalaia is known from two partial skull bones.
facts.quote: Although Oxalaia is known only from two partial skull bones

facts.statement: Oxalaia lived in a tropical, heavily forested habitat surrounded by an arid landscape.
facts.quote: Oxalaia habitat was tropical, heavily forested, and surrounded by an arid landscape.

facts.statement: Oxalaia had a partly piscivorous lifestyle similar to modern crocodilians.
facts.quote: As a spinosaurid, the traits of Oxalaia skull and dentition indicate a partly piscivorous (fish-eating) lifestyle similar to that of modern crocodilians.

facts.statement: Oxalaia fossils were recovered from the Laje do Coringa locality in 1999.
facts.quote: In 1999, fossils of Oxalaia were recovered from the Laje do Coringa.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen MN 6117-V consists of fused premaxillae from a large individual found in situ.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen of Oxalaia quilombensis, designated MN 6117-V, was found in situ (at its original place of deposition) with part of the left side embedded in the rock matrix; it consists of the fused premaxillae (frontmost snout bones) from a large individual.

facts.statement: An isolated left maxilla fragment designated MN 6119-V was referred to Oxalaia.
facts.quote: An isolated and incomplete left maxilla (main upper jaw bone) fragment (MN 6119-V) was referred to Oxalaia

facts.statement: The bone fragments were found on Cajual Island in Maranhão, Northeast Brazil.
facts.quote: Both bone fragments were found on Cajual Island, Maranhão, in the Northeast Region of Brazil

facts.statement: A fire in 2018 at the National Museum of Rio de Janeiro possibly destroyed Oxalaia specimens.
facts.quote: In 2018, a fire engulfed the palace housing the museum, possibly destroying Oxalaias specimens

facts.statement: Paleontologist Rubi Pêgas noted in 2025 that badly damaged Oxalaia remains were recovered.
facts.quote: It was noted by paleontologist Rubi Pêgas in 2025 that the badly damaged remains of Oxalaia were recovered

facts.statement: It is debated whether Oxalaia is a junior synonym of Spinosaurus or a distinct genus.
facts.quote: One study suggested that this taxon is a junior synonym of the closely related African genus Spinosaurus, but some subsequent studies consider the genus to be diagnostic.

facts.statement: The species description was written by Alexander Kellner, Elaine Machado, Sergio Azevedo, Deise Henriques, and Luciana Carvalho.
facts.quote: The species description of Oxalaia was written by Brazilian palaeontologists Alexander Kellner, Elaine Machado, Sergio Azevedo, Deise Henriques, and Luciana Carvalho.

facts.statement: The genus name Oxalaia is derived from the African deity Oxalá.
facts.quote: The generic name Oxalaia is derived from the name of the African deity Oxalá, which was introduced into Brazil during the slavery period.

facts.statement: The species name quilombensis refers to quilombo settlements founded by escaped slaves.
facts.quote: The specific name quilombensis refers to the quilombo settlements like those on Cajual Island, which were founded by escaped slaves.

facts.statement: The holotype premaxillae of Oxalaia measure approximately 201 mm in length, 115 mm in preserved width, and 103 mm in height.
facts.quote: The holotype premaxillae are together approximately 201 mm long, with a preserved width of 115 mm (maximal estimated original width is 126 mm), and a height of 103 mm.

facts.statement: Based on related spinosaurid skeletal material, the skull of Oxalaia is estimated to have been 1.35 meters long.
facts.quote: Based on skeletal material from related spinosaurids, the skull of Oxalaia would have been an estimated 1.35 m long

facts.statement: In 2011, Kellner and his team estimated Oxalaia to be between 12 and 14 meters long and weigh between 5 and 7 tonnes.
facts.quote: Kellner and his team compared the Dal Sasso specimen (MSNM V4047) to Oxalaia original snout in 2011; from this they estimated Oxalaia at 12 to 14 m in length and 5 to 7 t in weight

facts.statement: Oxalaia possesses a terminal rosette shape formed by an enlarged snout tip and a constricted rear end, a feature distinguishing spinosaurids.
facts.quote: The tip of the rostrum (snout) is enlarged and the rear-end constricted, forming the terminal rosette shape that distinguishes spinosaurids

facts.statement: The premaxillae of Oxalaia have seven tooth sockets on each side.
facts.quote: The premaxillae have seven alveoli (tooth sockets) on each side

facts.statement: A large gap separates the third and fourth tooth sockets in the tooth row of Oxalaia.
facts.quote: A large diastema (gap in tooth row) separates the third tooth socket from the fourth

facts.statement: Unlike its Early Cretaceous relatives Suchomimus and Cristatusaurus, Oxalaia lacked serrations on its teeth.
facts.quote: Small fragments inside some of the remaining alveoli show that unlike its Early Cretaceous relatives Suchomimus and Cristatusaurus, Oxalaia lacked serrations on its teeth

facts.statement: Oxalaia had two replacement teeth in each socket in addition to a single functional tooth.
facts.quote: Apart from the single, functional tooth in each socket, there were two replacement teeth

facts.statement: Kellner and colleagues differentiated Oxalaia from other spinosaurids based on distinguishing features such as sculptured palatal premaxillae and two replacement teeth per position.
facts.quote: Kellner and colleagues differentiated Oxalaia from it and other spinosaurids by its autapomorphic (distinguishing) craniodental features, like its sculptured palatal part of the premaxillae, and the possession of two replacement teeth in each position.

facts.statement: Oxalaia is assigned to the subfamily Spinosaurinae due to its upper jaw morphology and lack of fine tooth serrations typical of baryonychines.
facts.quote: Oxalaia is currently assigned to the subfamily Spinosaurinae due to the morphology of its upper jaw and the absence of fine serrations on its teeth that typify baryonychines.

facts.statement: In 2020, Smyth and colleagues argued that the distinguishing features of Oxalaia were insufficient for a separate taxon and resulted from individual variation.
facts.quote: In 2020, a paper by Robert Smyth and colleagues assessing spinosaurines from the Kem Kem Group did not find the autapomorphies of Oxalaia quilombensis sufficient to warrant a separate taxon, but instead considered them a result of individual variation.

facts.statement: Oxalaia lived during the Early Cretaceous, a time when its relatives Suchomimus and Cristatusaurus also existed.
facts.quote: unlike its Early Cretaceous relatives Suchomimus and Cristatusaurus, Oxalaia lacked serrations on its teeth

facts.statement: Oxalaia lived in a humid tropical forest habitat during the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: The Late Cretaceous deposits of the Alcântara Formation have been interpreted as a humid habitat of tropical forests dominated by conifers, ferns, and horsetails.

facts.statement: The forest habitat where Oxalaia lived was surrounded by an arid-to-semi-arid landscape with seasonal rainfall.
facts.quote: These forests were surrounded by an arid-to-semi-arid landscape that was probably subjected to brief periods of heavy rainfall followed by lengthy dry periods.

facts.statement: The only known fossils of Oxalaia were found in 1999 on Cajual Island within the Alcântara Formation.
